Right! 493 is on the board. Sri Lanka will now try to utilize the early morning conditions to strike early and push Bangladesh on the back foot. Bangladesh will hope that their openers start well and take them to a good position. Join us for Bangladesh's first innings in a short while.

You got to feel for the bowlers. The conditions were of no help for them. On the batting paradise, they had to work hard. They have bowled more than 170 overs and yet have failed to bundle out the hosts. Taskin bagged four wickets and he is their pick of the bowlers in this innings. However, he too had to work hard for it. Mehidy, Shoriful and Taijul managed to take one wicket apiece but they had to work hard for it.

Earlier in the game. Sri Lanka won the toss and decided to bat. Their openers, skipper Karunaratne and Thirimanne raked up their respective tons. Their number 3, Oshada too did well but missed out on his century. The middle-order failed but Dickwella did a great job to make sure Sri Lanka has got close to 500.

And Sri Lanka have declared here! Not sure what was on their mind. 24 runs added this morning. If the target was 500, they have not got there. If the idea was to see if Dickwella can get to his century, that's not happened, despite him being still there. He'd feel a bit unlucky as he was just 23 away and the way he was playing, he would've needed just 3-4 overs to get to his maiden Test ton. Not to be though but Sri Lanka have a big score.

Farveez Mahroof is in with the pitch report. Tells that it is really hot and humid. Adds that the wicket was really good to bat on the first 2 days. Adds that the cracks are opening up and a few balls spun too. Feels Sri Lanka will try to get to 500 and then make Bangladesh bat as quickly as possible. Tells that they need to use the conditions with the new ball.

Taskin Ahmed is caught for a little chat. He says that the last 2 years have been tough for him. Adds he has worked hard in these 2 years and he has learned a lot. Says it wasn't easy for him but it is all good for him. Tells that playing for the country is a dream and it is a joy to play. Says that he is following the process and keeping things simple at the moment. Adds that in conditions like these, bowling is tough but adds he is trying to give his best. Ends by saying that they always play to win but you cannot control the weather and pitches so all they can do is try their best.

Taskin was the man for Bangladesh who was getting them the wickets but without much support. Dickwella and Ramesh then took the attack to the bowlers and added 87 off just 117 balls with Dickwella scoring run-a-ball 64. Now, Sri Lanka would look to bat the first session and score as many runs as they can. Bangladesh, on the other hand, would be eager to close this innings as quickly as they can. Stay with us to find out how things pan out.

Hello and welcome all, to the moving day of the Test match between Bangladesh and Sri Lanka. On Day 2, it was once Sri Lanka who ran away with the show. Bangladesh did get 3 quick wickets in the first session of the day but they managed just 2 in the second with Oshada and Nissanka adding valuable runs.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Right then. Unfortunately for all of us, play has been cut short early on Day 2 due to a combination of bad light and rain, but that means that action on Day 3 will begin slightly earlier than usual. Sri Lanka will probably look to push past the 500-run mark and start off strongly with the ball, whereas, Bangladesh will want to bat as well as the hosts did. The action will begin at 0945 local (0415 GMT). We hope to have your company for Day 3. Until then, cheers and take care!

Sri Lanka will be pleased with their effort. They did not start the day as they would have wanted as they were made to toil hard for the runs. Oshada Fernando and Lahiru Thirimanne could not capitalize and convert their scores into massive ones. Angelo Mathews and Dhananjaya de Silva failed to get going. Nissanka too was unable to catch on his start. At 382/6, it looked like Bangladesh could bowl out the hosts for under 450. All those plans were down the drain though as Dickwella counter-attacked and forged a solid unbeaten stand of 87 with Ramesh Mendis which put the tourists back under the pump. The wicketkeeper-batsman is on 64 and has played with intent. It will be interesting to see whether he gets a chance to continue this effort on Day 3!

Unlike Day 1, it was a much better contest between bat and ball as the pitch has finally made batting, not a lot, but slightly challenging. Bangladesh started off the day well. They were nice and tight in the first session, did not allow Sri Lanka to score freely and also chipping in with wickets. Taskin Ahmed was the star as he scalped 3 wickets on the day and also had one put down off his bowling. Taijul and Mehidy were the other bowlers who got wickets. The former was good as he did get some purchase off the surface but the latter was unable to extract much off the deck.

So the inevitable has happened and the play has been called off for the day. It will be the tourists who will be the happier of the two sides as Dickwella was putting them under the sword and they would have probably had to bat the last hour. Sri Lanka would be rueing that they did not start the day well. The hosts though are still in a strong position in this game.

Oshada Fernando is looking solid and Sri Lanka would want him to carry on to score a ton. He is joined by Nissanka, who would look to score runs after getting out cheaply in the last Test. An exciting session awaits us after Lunch, make sure you join us for that!

Mickey Arthur is down for a chat, says that he is very happy with how Day 1 went. Thinks that this pitch will turn a little more and they will look to score more runs today. Adds that they are trying to be a team that is hard to beat and the cricket they have played in the last 3 Tests is of a high standard. Finishes by saying that will look to put on a big score today.

Hello and welcome to Day 2 of the second Test between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh. The hosts are well and truly on top of this game as they have made the most of the batting track. The pair of Thirimanne and Oshada will look to continue from where they left off on Day 1. Bangladesh bowlers had a tough outing in the field but they will look to find some inspiration. The pitch is a good one to bat on but the hosts need to find a way to make things difficult. Can the tourists bounce back in this game or will Sri Lanka continue their march with the bat?

Right! That is it from Day 1 of this match! Sri Lanka are in a strong position and would look to extend their score tomorrow. Bangladesh will look to take wickets with the new ball and then bat well. Do join us for Day 2 of this Test match. The action begins at 10:00 IST (4:30 GMT) on 30 April 2021. Till then, stay safe and take care!

Dimuth Karunaratne says that he never got back-to-back hundred and it feels great. Adds that he learned a lot of things during the West Indies tour. Tells that he has a good understanding with Lahiru Thirimanne as they have batted together since a young age. Says that there was nothing for the bowlers on this day but there might be something for spinners later on and adds that they are targeting 600 runs.

It was a very tough day for Bangladeshi bowlers. There was nothing in the pitch for them and they struggled to pick wickets. The biggest positive for them was the performance of Shoriful Islam. The debutant bowled with a big heart and picked up Dimuth Karunaratne. They have taken the second new ball and would look to make good use of it in the first hour tomorrow.

End of what has been a great day for Sri Lanka. They chose to bat and their openers, Lahiru Thirimanne and Dimuth Karunaratne feasted on these batting conditions. They both got to their hundreds and Sri Lanka did not lose a single wicket till Tea. Dimuth Karunaratne fell in the last session, but Oshada Fernando joined Lahiru Thirimanne and stitched a good partnership. There was a close call in the last over of the day but Lahiru Thirimanne survived it and they are in firm control at the end of Day 1. They will look to carry on tomorrow and put a big score on the board.

Loopy ball, outside off. Pushed away to covers.

200 up for Sri Lanka! Length ball, around off. Lahiru clips it wide of mid on. The fielder chases it and dives to stop it. But the batters have enough time to get back for the second.
Lands it on a length, on the fourth stump line. Lahiru Thirimanne defends it off the back foot.

We are back for the final session on Day 1. It is a very important session for Bangladesh because if they don't get wickets, they will be on the back foot at Stumps. Mehidy Hasan to start the proceedings. 16-3-46 for him so far.

One of the on-air commentators said that the Bangladeshi bowlers are at the mercy of the batsmen and he has been proven right in this session. They are bowling on a pitch that has nothing for them. There is a bit of turn but Lahiru and Dimuth are well equipped to deal with it. They need to try different things here. Bowl a few short ones, use the crease perhaps to break the monotony and get the first wicket. But will they be able to do so? All your questions will be answered in the final session of Day 1. Stay tuned for that...

The story for Sri Lanka so far in the Test has been the same as the first Test. Dimuth Karunaratne and Lahiru Thirimanne have feasted on this pitch. They have given minimal chances to the bowlers and have scored boundaries at will in this session. The skipper continued his great form and has got to a well-deserved ton here. Lahiru Thirimannehas also batted excellently and is looking set to get his century too. They have plenty of batting to come and these two will look to finish the day without any loss.
Outside off, punched towards the bowler. TEA ON DAY 1!
Around middle, worked towards square leg.

EDGED, FOUR! Life is so cruel if you are a fast bowler and your name is not Glenn McGrath. Outside off, on a length, moving away, induces the error from Lahiru Thirimanne. He pokes at it, aiming to steer it behind point but to his luck, the outside edge goes between first slip and gully to third man! Moves to 80 now, does Thirimanne.

CENTURY FOR DIMUTH KARUNARATNE! Make hay when the sun shines, goes the saying. He is making hay and baking bread along with ploughing the field as well. Nothing happening on the pitch and Karunaratne has feasted. Gets there by using his feet and flicking it wide of long on. Comes back for the second. There comes the raise of the bat. Farveez Maharoof on air informs us that this is the first time that KARUNARATNE HAS SCORED CONSECUTIVE CENTURIES! Kudos, skipper.
Around middle, short in length, punched through mid-wicket for a single. Over to you, skip...

Now, now, now, Lahiru, why would you do that? Taking a single off the last ball? Shouldn't your skipper be hogging the strike right now? Length ball, outside off, eased through the covers for a single.

Outside off, pushed through cover-point for a single to move to 98...

I love you, Taskin. This is what Dimuth Karunaratne would be saying in his mind. He is in the 90s, with the clock ticking towards Tea and there will be the wish to get to that ton before Tea. And here he gets a buffet, down the leg side. He flicks it through backward square leg where fine leg gets across to his right, dives and parries it to deep square leg. Two runs taken, three more needed...

15 minutes to go to Tea. Mominul Haque reverts to pace. Taskin Ahmed is back in the attack. 10-1-37-0 for him so far. Can he get the first wicket here? A slip and a gully are waiting...

We are back for the second session! Sri Lanka will look to motor along and Bangladesh are in search of their first wicket. Abu Jayed will start the proceedings post lunch. 6-2-10-0 for him so far

Not a lot in the surface for the Bangladesh bowlers. They did bowl tight but without any success. There was a chance crated of Karunaratne but it wasn’t taken. However, they need to continue to be patient and keep hitting the right lengths. Will they have some success after the break? We will find out.

A solid session for Sri Lanka! Yes, they have scored at a slow rate but they haven’t lost a wicket. Also, the discipline with which Bangladesh have bowled is also a reason of them not scoring quickly. The openers are once again laying a foundation for a big first innings score. More of the same is what Lanka will want after the break. They though will hope the two can score a little quickly.

Goos length and on off, DK  hangs back and pushes it to mid off.

Shorter and outside off, Karunaratne slashes at it but misses.

Drinks Break! It has been a good hour of Test cricket. Bangladesh have bowled probing lines and have tested the Sri Lankan batters. Lahiru Thirimanne and Dimuth Karunaratne have done well too and have rarely given any chances to the bowlers. Bangladesh would look to break this partnership soon and the debutant, Shoriful Islam, might get the wicket as he bowled very well.

The Sri Lanka openers stride out to the middle. Dimuth Karunaratne and Lahiru Thirimanne will open for them. It will be Abu Jayed who uses the red cherry first. Here we go....

Mominul Haque, the Bangladesh skipper, says he also wanted to bat first. States the wicket won’t be the same and the spinners might game some turn later on. Informs they have one change, Shoriful Islam comes in for Ebadat Hossain.

Dimuth Karunaratne, the Sri Lanka skipper, says the wicket is very good for the first few days and later on there might be something for the bowlers. Informs that Ramesh Mendis and Praveen Jayawickrama make their way in the side. Says that Praveen Jayawickrama is making his Test debut.

PITCH REPORT - Aamer Sohail is down for the pitch report, says that the pitch is slightly different as it doesn't have the grass covering. Adds that there is a bit of moisture here but it is very hard and should be good for batting. Tells that there are cracks and with time it might open up and help the bowlers to pick up wickets.
Bangladesh (Playing XI) - Tamim Iqbal, Saif Hassan, Najmul Hossain Shanto, Mominul Haque (C), Mushfiqur Rahim, Liton Das (WK), Mehidy Hasan, Taijul Islam, Taskin Ahmed, Shoriful Islam, Abu Jayed

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Dimuth Karunaratne (C), Lahiru Thirimanne, Oshada Fernando, Angelo Mathews, Dhananjaya de Silva, Pathum Nissanka, Niroshan Dickwella (WK), Ramesh Mendis, Suranga Lakmal, Vishwa Fernando, Praveen Jayawickrama
TOSS - Sri Lanka have won the toss and they have chosen to bat first.

Given that the game is being played at the same venue, there could be an instance of the deck getting slower. That should mean toss could play a crucial role. Sri Lanka have not won a home series SINCE 2018, while Bangladesh too, have not done that well. Augurs well for desperation.

Zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz. Zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz. Zzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzzz. This was the state of all those who were covering the Opening Test, right from the second hour of Day 1. The batsmen batted, and batted, and batted and kept on batting. The bowlers toiled hard, trying to find a wicket similar to finding a pin in a dusty room. The curator came under a lot of scanner for producing such a pitch and given that the second game is also at this venue, the expectations would be that this would be a result-oriented pitch. But will reality meet expectations? Hello and a warm welcome to the second Test between Sri Lanka and Bangladesh at Pallekele. Stay tuned for toss and more updates...
